about: What Shree-Lipi's own composers write for Unicode Odia: S8OriU64.dll (Unicode) and S8Ori764.dll (Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes), Shree-Lipi nxt, typed the same keys into both (capture r3\cap-ori, 2026-10-18: the 8 vendor .ORI keyboards and 1,203 probe keyboards, every capture run twice, identical). Each row: the Unicode string, the preferred bytes (hex, one byte per glyph code) and, when there are any, the other spellings the composer also accepts. Canonical typing order only (the e-sign struck first, ୈ ୋ ୌ as େ + letter + ୖ / ା / ୗ, the reph struck after its syllable and before ଂ ଁ ଃ, ra-/ya-phala with their own codes, conjuncts through the link code); the other orders and the composer's quirks are kept in the capture, not here. The bytes are what the shree-ori7 table writes for SHREE-ORI7-0600..0604 and SHREE-ORI-0600..0604 (the same codes in both families): the composer's raw bytes with the corrections in byteMap and exceptions. tools/OriTruth builds and checks the shree-ori7 tables against it.

byteMap.9C: 5B - the composer's raw byte for ନ is 9C; every installed face (S0600892-S0604892, S06000F2-S06040F2, WORI7001/2) draws the ligature ଙ୍କ୍ତ at 9C (U+0153, 566/1000 wide) and ନ at 5B (341 wide; 5B FF is as wide as କ 4C FF). Rendered: r3\tbl-ori\round1\glyphs3.png, sheet-00..02.png. 1427 rows carry ନ and are written with 5B; the reverse tables read a bare 9C as ଙ୍କ୍ତ, the glyph a document shows there, and 9C FF - ନ as the composer writes it, which is the only place it writes 9C - as ନ.

exceptions: P3b: the composer writes 3C, which only WORI7001/2 draw as ₹ (SHREE-ORI7-0600..0602 and SHREE-ORI-* have no 3C; Word shows its fallback '<'); passed through as itself, reported - Ctrl+Shift+1 then $ keeps typing ₹

P3b: the composer writes 8F, which the fonts hold at U+008F, a C1 control Word and RichEdit draw as nothing (r3\word\final-invisible.txt), and no other code point of the fonts reaches that glyph; passed through as itself, reported
P3b: the composer writes 90 (U+0090, a C1 control Word and RichEdit draw as nothing; no other code point reaches the glyph); passed through as itself, reported
